newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down sharply at 8.2994 against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2960 due to intervention by the central bank and profit-taking, dealers said.
They said intervention at the opening by the People's Bank of China halted possible rises due to China's increasing trade surplus and that this was followed by profit-taking.
China posted a trade surplus of $3.91 billion in October and $12.01 billion in the first 10 months of 1996.
The yuan opened down at an intra-day high of 8.2970 and fell to consolidate around 8.2980, before hitting a low of 8.2996.
Trading was active, with most done at 8.2980, traders said.
"Usually a higher trade surplus data is good news for the yuan," said one dealer. "But this surplus was expected, so the news had been digested in the past few days," he added.
"Some banks bought the yuan early this week and sold it at higher levels today to take profits," a second dealer said.
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.2980 on Thursday.
The yuan closed up at 7.4250 from 7.4505 against 100 Japanese yen and down slightly at 1.0730 from 1.0725 against the Hong Kong dollar.
